title: Avoiding the Reverse Fall Mistake in Waste Pipes
description: One of the most frequent errors in drainage installations is failing to maintain a consistent downward slope on horizontal waste pipes, often leading to a condition known as reverse fall. When a pipe lacks proper slope or sags over time, wastewater cannot drain efficiently by gravity. Instead, solid waste settles in the low spots, causing recurring blockages and slow drains. Professional installers always verify alignment using a spirit level and secure adequate support hangers along the entire run to prevent mid-span sagging. Correcting this error during rough-in saves hours of future troubleshooting and prevents property damage.

Avoiding the Reverse Fall Mistake in Waste Pipes

One of the most frequent errors in drainage installations is failing to maintain a consistent downward slope on horizontal waste pipes, often leading to a condition known as reverse fall. When a pipe lacks proper slope or sags over time, wastewater cannot drain efficiently by gravity. Instead, solid waste settles in the low spots, causing recurring blockages and slow drains. Professional installers always verify alignment using a spirit level and secure adequate support hangers along the entire run to prevent mid-span sagging. Correcting this error during rough-in saves hours of future troubleshooting and prevents property damage.
